correctness.rationale: For p prime, t>=1, q=p^t, odd n>=3, curve y^(q²)−y=x^m with m=(q^n+1)/(q+1), the pole weights at infinity and genus g=(q−1)(q^n−q)/2 give a holomorphic monomial basis. The chosen b=(q^(n−1)−1)/(q+1) is integral, and ω=x^(p^(t−1)b−1)y^(p^(t−1))dx has pole order ≤2g−2. Apply the explicit monomial Cartier rule: t−1 y-exponent reductions, one transition −x^(p^(t(n−1)−1)−1)dx, then t(n−1)−1 further x reductions yield C^(tn−1)(ω)=−dx ≠0 (sign equals + in characteristic 2). The general upper bound C^(tn)=0 follows by cited Garcia–Tafazolian theorem 3.3 for this ABQ family maximal over F_(q^(2n)). Thus nilpotency index is exactly tn, not merely a bound. Independent finite exact witness-chain arithmetic checked six (p,t,n) triples including (2,2,3),(3,2,3),(5,1,3) and confirms scalar −1 mod p. Finite checks do not certify full upper bound, which is a prior published theorem.
